clue.text: Finish the whole affair and drink neat gin?

definitions.meaning: to finish with something completely and put it behind you
gin and It is gin with Italian vermouth; taking gin neat is drinking it without the It

explanation.surface: Someone ending an affair and reaching for a straight gin to mark it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a pun: 'gin and It' is gin mixed with Italian vermouth, so neat gin is literally gin taken without the It.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to finish something entirely and stop bothering with it.

clue.text: Cricket ground with duck leading to endless depression

indicators.note: the duck comes first and leads on to what follows

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: the word for depression loses its final letter

parts.note: a vale is a valley, a dip in the land

explanation.surface: A cricket ground where a batter's duck leads to endless gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last E of VALE. THE OVAL is a famous London cricket ground; 'depression' suggests gloom but means a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oval in Kennington, south London, is a Test cricket venue.

clue.text: Time to get a little sunshine — one may come with some tea

definitions.text: one may come with some tea

parts.note: a ray is a single beam, a little bit of sunshine

explanation.surface: Waiting for a bit of sun before taking afternoon tea outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is often brought on a flat board with a rim, carrying the cups and pot.

clue.text: Like a kind of energy that gets old cows twitching

parts.note: kine is an archaic plural of cow
a tic is an involuntary twitching of a muscle

explanation.surface: Some form of energy makes elderly cattle jerk about.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy of motion is so called in physics, contrasted with potential energy.

clue.text: Most successful rep gets a popular book

parts.note: best means most successful, top of the field
a sales rep is a seller of goods

explanation.surface: The top sales representative wins a well-liked novel as a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A book that sells in huge numbers and tops the charts is widely popular.

clue.text: Robot-like as Bottom, say, in A Midsummer Night's Dream

definitions.meaning: acting automatically, without thought, like a machine

definitions.text: as Bottom, say, in A Midsummer Night's Dream
definitions.meaning: Bottom and his fellow tradesmen are called the rude ... in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: Describing the stiff acting of Bottom in the Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's amateur actors in the play, workmen like Bottom the weaver, are known as the 'rude mechanicals'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes automatic, machine-like action, and in its noun form names a manual workman in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Seven matters I'd written about in notices for the press?

indicators.note: the letters of these words are written out again in a different order

explanation.surface: An editor has written up seven topics in notices sent to the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' rearranges SEVEN MATTERS ID, all fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverts are paid notices placed in newspapers, the press, to sell things.

clue.text: Transport items? Simple — relax!

parts.note: to transport something is to take it somewhere
items are things
simple means easy

explanation.surface: A removals job looks simple, so the mover is told to calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to rest and not exert yourself, which is to unwind.

clue.text: Stratagem needed by this person sunk in depression in military manoeuvre

indicators.note: the stratagem and the speaker are sunk into the hollow, placed inside it

parts.note: a dent is a small depression in a surface
a ploy is a cunning stratagem
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A cunning plan needed by a commander bogged down in a hollow during a battle exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Spreading troops into position for action is a military movement of forces.

clue.text: Resistance unit set up in Nottingham house

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are read upwards, backwards
the letters sit inside the words Nottingham house

explanation.surface: An electrical resistor was installed in a house in Nottingham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' hides MHO across nottinghaM HOuse; 'set up' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of electrical resistance is named after Georg Simon Ohm.

clue.text: Fish in tremulous motion, first to get away

indicators.note: the initial letter of the word for tremulous motion leaves

parts.note: a shake is a trembling movement

explanation.surface: A fish trembling on the line, the first one to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to get away' removes the S from SHAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cod-family sea fish common on European menus.

clue.text: The deep chair maybe with no back

indicators.note: the final letter, the back of the word, is removed

parts.note: a chair is an example of a seat

explanation.surface: A deep armchair, perhaps, that has no backrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no back' drops the T from SEAT; the 'deep' looks like part of the chair's description.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep is a poetic name for the ocean.

clue.text: Go around northernmost place in Ireland — finally locate valuable mineral

parts.note: to tour a place is to go around it
Malin Head in County Donegal is the most northerly point of the island of Ireland

indicators.note: only the last letter of locate is taken

explanation.surface: A prospector travels round the far north of Ireland to find a precious mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: Malin Head is Ireland's northernmost point.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a crystalline boron silicate prized as a gemstone in many colours.

clue.text: What gets sailor up above deck, one being stranded

definitions.text: What gets sailor up above deck, one being stranded

parts.words: What gets sailor up above deck, one being stranded
parts.note: a climbing aid on ships made of rope; stranded means made of twisted strands rather than marooned

explanation.surface: A shipwrecked sailor, stranded somewhere, needs a way to climb up above deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranded' suggests marooned but means made of strands, as rope is.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing device with rungs strung between cords, used on ships to go aloft.

clue.text: A planetoid, no place having phone or vehicle

indicators.note: the abbreviation for place is removed from the planetoid

parts.note: Pluto is now classed as a dwarf planet
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
a mobile is a mobile phone

explanation.surface: A space rock with nowhere to land and a phone, or a spacecraft perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes PL from PLUTO, leaving UTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is a motor vehicle; the longer word is its formal name.

clue.text: Bananas and crunchy food

definitions.meaning: hard-shelled kernels such as almonds or walnuts

explanation.surface: A snack of fruit together with something crunchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both bananas and the answer are slang for mad, and the answer also names crunchy kernels.

clue.text: Hesitation about bad feeling — give me a break!

indicators.note: the hesitation word is turned about, read backwards

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
spite is ill will, bad feeling

explanation.surface: Someone sick of dithering and bad blood pleads for some peace.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause or short interval of relief from something unpleasant is a break.

clue.text: Lax female, the Parisian caught by detectives

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A careless Frenchwoman is arrested by plain-clothes police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught by detectives' puts C beside CID, not inside it. The CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: Lax means slack or loose, and the answer means limp and lacking firmness.

clue.text: Having regular contact off the field

definitions.meaning: in rugby and football, a ball that has gone over the touchline off the playing area is said to be so

explanation.surface: Staying connected with someone even when not playing.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby, a ball over the touchline has left the field of play.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means staying in communication, and in sport describes a ball beyond the touchline.

clue.text: The Bard's determination

definitions.meaning: the Bard is Shakespeare, whose first name is a short form of William

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's resolve, or perhaps his famous testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's short first name doubles as a word for resolve.

clue.text: One girl, May, works in a branch of earth sciences

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A girl called May works in a department of geology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' rearranges ONE GIRL MAY; it looks like her job.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the study of minerals, a discipline within the earth sciences.

clue.text: Like son who lacks wisdom?

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of

explanation.surface: Asking whether a son resembles someone foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey is a byword for stupidity, so the word names a fool.

clue.text: Past ace has to give way

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards
to go is to collapse, give way

explanation.surface: A former star player must now step aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Used after a time, the word means back in the past, as in years before now.

clue.text: Get rid of garden feature?

definitions.meaning: to cast off, as a snake its skin
a wooden hut in the garden for tools

explanation.surface: Asking whether to clear away something in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to cast off, and the noun is a small garden hut for storage.

clue.text: Paper shows way the woman entered into risky venture

indicators.note: the way and the woman go inside the word for a risky venture

parts.note: a bet is a gamble
a road is a way
she refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Newspaper reveals how a woman got caught up in a dangerous scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A large-format serious newspaper is called this, contrasted with a tabloid.

clue.text: Wood somewhere in Kent

definitions.meaning: pine or fir timber, sawn into planks
a coastal town in the English county of Kent

explanation.surface: Timber from a forest somewhere in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; the town is on its coast near Dover.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names softwood timber and also a seaside town in Kent.

clue.text: It sounds like he would take notice

indicators.note: tells us the answer is said like the contraction of the next words

parts.note: he would contracts to he'd

explanation.surface: Apparently he would pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay attention to advice is to mind it; the verb is a synonym of noticing.

clue.text: Horses escape shelters, going wild

indicators.note: the letters run wild and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Horses break out of their stables and run amok.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses that race over fences and ditches in jump racing are given this name.
